description:
About the Position

Utrecht University's School of Economics invites applications for an Assistant Professor in Economics. The position combines research, teaching and organisational duties within an economics department known for work on international economics, sustainability, development and institutions, and offers a route through the university's tenure-track system.

The assistant professor develops an independent research agenda, publishes in international peer-reviewed journals, acquires or contributes to external research funding, and teaches in the school's bachelor's and master's programmes. Supervision of student theses and participation in the academic life of the department form part of the role, with reduced teaching loads in the early years supported by mentoring.

Candidate Profile

Applicants hold a PhD in economics or a closely related field (or are close to completion) and demonstrate strong research potential in at least one of the school's focus areas. Teaching experience at university level and evidence of high-quality teaching are expected. The appointment follows the Utrecht University tenure-track conditions with a competitive salary on the Dutch university scales, and the application deadline is fixed.

Highlights

  • Independent research in economics
  • Publication in international peer-reviewed journals
  • Teaching in bachelor's and master's programmes
  • External funding and grant participation
  • Tenure-track development with mentoring
  • Faculty appointment at the Utrecht School of Economics

About Utrecht University

Utrecht University is a leading Dutch research university, consistently ranked among the top institutions in Europe. Its research and teaching span four faculties and a broad range of strategic themes, including sustainability, dynamics of youth, institutions for open societies and life sciences. PhD candidates and postdocs in the Netherlands are salaried staff members with full employment benefits under the CAO-NU collective agreement, so advertised positions are fully funded. Academic and support vacancies are published on the university's working-at portal, with clear deadlines and application instructions per position.

Official details: Read the programme or project information

Application route: Follow the official application instructions

Contact

Questions about this position, eligibility or the application process should be raised through the contact channel given on the official announcement page (see the Official Link section above). Always quote the position reference in your message so the admissions or HR team can route your enquiry quickly.

Important Notes

  • Application deadline: 15 November 2026 - late or incomplete applications are normally not considered.
  • Listing details were recorded from the official source at the time of publication; always confirm the latest requirements on the official page before applying.
  • Prepare the documents listed in the eligibility and application sections before starting the online form - transcripts, CV and references take the longest to collect.

How to Apply

Submit your application through the official page before the deadline: 15 November 2026. Read the eligibility requirements carefully and prepare all requested documents - early applications are strongly recommended for competitive awards.

Open the official application page ↗

Application guides

  • How to Email a PhD Supervisor: 7 Templates and Practical Tips
  • How to Read a PhD Job Advert: Funding, Eligibility and Application Steps

English language requirements

No IELTS or TOEFL certificate is requested for this employed Dutch position; English is assessed through the application documents and an interview in English.
